Through 165 companies, it used to do business in 53 countries. It sold baby products to pharmaceuticals listed as essential items by WHO. It had cordial relations with the media too. Employees were happy working with the company. On 30th September 1982, media reported that there were deaths due to intake of extra strength Tylenol from Chicago area. CEO James Burke was alerted by the staff of the company. At that time, there was no crisis communication plan with the company. McNeil is subsidiary of Johnson & Johnson. It manufactures Tylenol in U.S. There was fear among the executives of the company as no company faced this sort of situation before. ‘ A seven-member Crisis Management Group(CMG) was setup. With the approval of James Burke, the team recalled Tylenol capsules from Chicago area stores. They found that cyanide was the cause of death. Recalled batches of Tylenol capsules were tested and cyanide was found in two capsules. CMG was puzzled with the presence of cyanide in capsules. The company immediately warned the public not to take Tylenol capsules. CMG identified key stakeholders to communicate. 1) Medical professionals 2) Consumers (Media) 3) Internal members of the company i.e., employees and other groups.4) Food and Drug Administration. All-important HT stakeholders were kept in touch with continuously. 33 telephortés were installed by the company to communicate to the public. Toll-free telephone lines were kept open to gather information from the public. Messages were continuously analyzed and-updated. Also, they remained in continuous contact with media that continuously carried the story. Full-page advertisements were given in all newspapers in Chicago area that company would exchange Tylenol capsules with Tylenol tablets. Empioyees were informed about latest developments in crisis management. They were shown the plan to tackle the crisis. Also, Communication was sent through electronic devices to external stakeholders. They in turn shared with distributors, retailers and medical professionals. Because of the crisis Tylenol capsules were discontinued from production. Within the 10 weeks of crisis, tamper-proof, triple sealed safety containers were put in retail shelves. Moreover, Johnson & Johnson worked closely with local police, FBI and Food and Drug Administration to find out the culprit. FBI and FDA investigation didn’t yield any results. The person responsible for Tylenol crisis was not found. The company declared $1,00,000 reward for helping the murderer to be found. Nobody though claimed the reward. . CMG’s aim was to regain confidence of the public and resale products to them. As they ran the crises management campaign, there was no sales impact on other Johnson &Johnson products. Consumers didn’t boycott the company. Though the entire crises management costed $100 million to the company it resulted in regaining 100% market share of Tylenol. -| On 11th October,1982 Washington Post wrote in front page praising Johnson & Johnson for swift crisis response: “Johnson & Johnson has effectively demonstrated how a major business ought to handle a disaster...” > oe Johnson & Johnson spokesperson mentioned three reasons for successfully coping with the crisis:1) The company was transparent with the media.
